transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because I've been having some trouble keeping up with conversations. I volunteer at the local museum, and lately, people will be talking right to me—maybe about the upcoming art walk or something like that—and I’ll be looking right at them. But then I realize I completely missed the middle of what they were saying. I end up having to ask them to run it by me again. It's just getting a bit frustrating.
Does this trouble understanding what people are saying happen more when it's noisy or crowded, or does it happen even when you're in a quiet room with just one other person talking clearly?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't noticed if it's worse when there's a lot of background noise or a crowd. It seems to happen even when it's just me and another person talking in a quiet room. I just... lose track of what they're saying regardless of what's going on around us.
Is this difficulty following conversations something new that's developed recently, or has this been a pattern for you since childhood or early adulthood?

Well, it's definitely not a new thing. It's been a pattern for a long time, honestly. Even back in grade school, my report cards would always say things like "daydreams" or "needs reminders to finish work." I remember my mother used to have to sit right beside me just to keep me on track with my homework... at least until I was about twelve or so. So, yeah, it's been going on since I was a kid.
Besides missing parts of conversations, do you also notice yourself losing focus or forgetting things while doing other tasks, like at work, managing bills, or organizing your day-to-day activities?

Yeah, I do notice it with other things, too. Like when I'm reading. I can sit down with a gallery packet for the museum or just a set of notes, and I'll start out fine. But after a few minutes... my eyes keep moving over the page, but my mind has completely wandered off somewhere else. I end up having to go back and read the exact same part all over again just to actually take it in.
Do you also notice yourself feeling restless, acting impulsively, or having trouble staying organized in multiple areas of your life, like at home, work, or in social situations?

No, I wouldn't say I feel restless or act impulsively. I mean, I don't feel like I have to be moving all the time or anything like that. And I don't really do things without thinking them through. As for being disorganized... I don't think it's a major problem across the board. It's really just the focus part, like with the reading or the conversations, that I notice.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a longstanding (since childhood) pattern of inattention: difficulty sustaining attention in conversations and reading, being easily distracted, and a childhood history of inattentive symptoms (daydreaming, needing reminders, requiring parental supervision to complete homework until age 12). These symptoms are pervasive across settings (social conversations, reading/work tasks) and are not better explained by hearing difficulty, since symptoms occur even in quiet, one-on-one settings. No hyperactive-impulsive symptoms (restlessness, impulsivity, disorganization) are endorsed, indicating a predominantly inattentive presentation consistent with ADHD (F90.0). Hearing loss (H91.9) was considered but ruled out as symptoms are not exacerbated by noise/crowds and are context-independent. Other neurodevelopmental/learning disorders (F98.8) were considered but insufficient evidence given the clear, longstanding inattentive symptom cluster meeting ADHD criteria.
